instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Choose What Matters More
cards.instruction: Make someone choose between emotional safety and the outcome they claim to want.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's your audition number. Put the music in order, please. We're either going through that door or taking you home.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I want the part. I don't want them laughing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Those are separate requirements. I can help you sing the first line; I cannot train the panel's faces. Which are we working on?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Walk me in, but promise I won't freeze.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No one can promise that. Mark your starting note, please. I can stay where you can see me. Will you sing with that help, or shall we leave?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we renew the lease, choose what you want from this dinner: my honest view of living together, or reassurance. Please don't ask for both.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Honesty. Just don't say anything that makes me panic.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That isn't an instruction I can carry out. You can set the pace, not pre-approve the answer. Shall I begin?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Start by saying we're fine.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's still an answer, not a pace. Try 'one sentence at a time'. Or we can order dinner and leave the lease unsigned tonight.

cards.title: Stay for the Hard Part
cards.instruction: Create increasing moments of emotional honesty to test whether someone remains present and supportive.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave the laptop shut, please. I haven't booked our anniversary trip, and searching flights before hearing me would be a mistake.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I thought you just needed help finding cheap seats.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I let you think that. Please don't solve the price; I was relieved when the cheap seats sold out. Can you listen to the rest?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Is it the trip you don't want, or us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Us. I'm not sure I want to stay together. Don't offer a different destination, please. Sit beside me while I try to say this properly.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: About the reunion: please don't explain my late arrival as traffic. I was outside for half an hour. Let me explain it properly.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I saved you a seat. I thought you didn't want to sit with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the wrong conclusion. I wanted that seat. I saw you laughing with everyone and couldn't make myself come in.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was telling them about our camping trip. I wanted you there to finish the story.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Please don't dismiss this: I thought you'd be happier without me. Will you sit with me while I tell you how long I've believed that?

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Drop the Armor
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to lower their guard, stop performing strength, or admit what affects them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The shop's locked. You can stop the cheerful voice now. Please put the till drawer down; counting it a third time won't add a customer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Someone has to keep morale up. You're my only employee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've clocked off. You're addressing a friend now, not staff. Start again: how did today feel?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I cried in the stockroom. Then I practised smiling before you came back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: No more rehearsal, please. Sit here, where you don't have to hide. You can tell me about the stockroom without putting that voice back on.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've said you're managing three times over dinner. That's a conclusion, not an answer. What happens when you get home?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I put the television on so the flat sounds occupied.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then invite me. Directly, please. You don't need to persuade me the flat is too quiet.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come tomorrow. I'll cook something nice. I promise I won't be miserable.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remove the promise and ask again. I'll come for toast and whatever mood you're actually in.

cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: I Started the Spiral
cards.instruction: Hide how much your own fear or resentment created the emotional crisis while helping everyone calm it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our message to the stallholders needs to be calm and accurate: the fair is going ahead. Please remove the word 'panic'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You panicked about the forecast and told them to cancel their vans.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The forecast has improved. Put that first. I'll ring the transport firms; please don't turn the update into a discussion of my tone.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Two vans are cancelled. They need to know who's replacing them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the two names; I'll arrange replacements. Write 'transport being reorganised', please. Leave my earlier calls out of the update.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The club money was in the other envelope. Please change your committee message from 'missing funds' to 'balance confirmed'.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You phoned me crying that the treasurer had stolen it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Which is why we must be precise now. State the amount, not the accusation. I'll count it again with you before you send anything.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They've already asked the treasurer to come in and explain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then ring them, please. Say there's no need for that meeting; the balance is correct. I'll speak if they have questions about the amount. Questions about the call can wait.

cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Not the Real Fear
cards.instruction: Keep the conversation focused on practical details so no one reaches the fear underneath them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before I open the scholarship letter, please put the tea on saucers. Not beside the envelope; paper and hot drinks need separate areas.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've moved the cups. Open it. I want to know if you're leaving.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: There's still sugar beside it. Clear the sugar away, please. A clean surface means the whole surface.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll hold the letter. Are you scared of going, or of staying here with me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Hold it by the edges, please. Not over the cup. If we're doing this in the kitchen, at least let me clear a proper place for you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before we discuss me moving out, read the departure time back to me. The train time, please, not when we should leave the house.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Six twelve. Fifth time I've checked. Your ticket's in your hand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Now the barrier: don't tell me the booking reference will open it. I need the actual code ready.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll walk you through. Are you frightened of leaving me?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you need to check your own access. Please don't join the queue until we know whether you're allowed onto the platform without a ticket.
